name: blueline-speed
works_with: Agent Skills format, tested with Claude Code and Codex. Helper scripts need Node.js 22 or later
short: Finds why a marketing page is slow and what to fix first, with evidence for every finding.
what: A page speed review skill from blueline, covering its laws 8 and 9: your page loads first, and media is prepared once and cached. It checks Core Web Vitals from real-user data, render-blocking and third-party scripts, JavaScript weight, fonts, the main image, layout shifts, caching, image formats and sizes, lazy loading and video. Two Node scripts collect facts as JSON, and the agent writes a fixed-shape report where every finding quotes a command output, file line or page text.
who: Developers and marketers who run a marketing site and want a prioritized list of speed fixes. Skip it if you want a full site review, which the main blueline skill covers, or if you want automatic fixes without a review first.
needs: A coding agent that supports Agent Skills. The README names Claude Code and Codex
A shell. Checks on a live site need network access
Node.js 22 or later for the helper scripts. Without Node, the references give equivalent curl commands
Optional: a CrUX API key in an environment variable for real-user speed data. Without it, the skill says to use PageSpeed Insights in a browser
Optional: an agent with a browser, for checks that compare raw and rendered HTML or need the first screen

steps.title: Install from your project folder
steps.text: This installs all six blueline skills. Add -g for all your projects, or -s with a skill name to install only one. Each skill carries its own references and scripts, so blueline-speed can be installed on its own.

steps.title: Call the skill
steps.text: Use /blueline-speed <url> in Claude Code or $blueline-speed <url> in Codex, or ask in plain words about page speed.

steps.title: Or run the scripts yourself
steps.text: Run them from the skill's folder. Each prints JSON facts and signals.
steps.code:
node scripts/page.mjs https://www.example.com/            # scripts in the head, stylesheets, fonts, images in order, video, cache headers
node scripts/assets.mjs https://www.example.com/          # JavaScript and CSS weight, image formats, sizes, cache lifetimes

try.label: From the README
try.text: /blueline-speed <url> in Claude Code, or $blueline-speed <url> in Codex. Replace <url> with a site you own or may review.

watch: The scripts send GET and HEAD requests to the site under review and do not apply robots.txt. They go one request at a time with delays. Review only sites you own or may review.
Some fallback curl commands save page.html in the current folder.
The skill reviews first and changes nothing until you ask. Then it fixes one finding at a time.
Google guidance quoted in the references was checked on 30 September 2026. Newer changes are not covered.
The README says the checks do not guarantee rankings, AI citations or traffic.
